title: Metagenomic Characterization of Rhizosphere PGPR Siderophore Production in Organic Substrates
description: PhD dissertation investigating Bacillus velezensis and Pseudomonas fluorescens pyoverdine siderophore chelation, iron bioavailability, and root disease suppression in organic CEA.
image_caption: 16S rRNA metagenomic sequencing profile of beneficial rhizosphere bacterial populations in organic coco coir substrate.
overview: Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria (PGPR) enhance iron (Fe) availability in substrate hydroponics by secreting high-affinity iron-chelating molecules called siderophores (e.g., pyoverdine). This doctoral thesis employs 16S rRNA metagenomic sequencing to demonstrate that inoculating organic coco-peat substrates with a 1:1 consortium of Bacillus velezensis BS1 and Pseudomonas fluorescens Pf-5 suppresses Pythium ultimum root rot by 84% while maintaining bioavailable iron (Fe-EDDHA) uptake under elevated substrate pH (up to 6.8).

climate_strategy.strategy: Inoculate substrate reservoirs bi-weekly with PGPR consortium at 10⁶ CFU/mL. Maintain substrate temperature at 21.5°C to promote bacterial biofilm formation around root elongation zones.

crop_steering.intro: Rhizosphere microbiome and pathogen exclusion steering matrix.

fertigation.intro: Organic fertigation and iron chelation management.
fertigation.vegetative_phase: Supply Iron-EDDHA (Fe 25 µM) alongside organic carbon exudates (humic/fulvic acids 5 mg/L) to stimulate PGPR siderophore synthesis.
fertigation.generative_phase: Maintain substrate pH between 5.8 and 6.5 to ensure stability of pyoverdine-Fe complexes.

references.text: Metagenomic analysis of PGPR siderophore production and Pythium root rot suppression in organic hydroponics.
